texts.preamble: State vs Juned Ahmed on 25 October, 2025 In The Court Of Sh. Ankit Garg Jmfc-08 Phc/Nd Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Cr case no. 8757/2020 State Vs. Juned Ahmed Ps Delhi Cantt U/s 279/337 Ipc Judgment
texts.facts: The case of the prosecution as unfolded by the police report is that on 07.12.2019, at around 11:20 PM underpass in front of Domestic Airport, within the jurisdiction of P.S. Delhi Cantt. Accused was driving the offending vehicle registration bearing no. HR 74A 4354 in a manner so rash or negligent so as to endanger human life and personal safety of others and thereby he committed an offence punishable under Section 279 IPC. Secondly, on the aforesaid date, time and place, while driving the aforesaid vehicle in the aforesaid manner, hit against one vehicle no. DL 10CL 7826 and caused a grievous injury to Prahlad Singh thereby he committed an offence punishable u/s 337 IPC. On the basis of the charge-sheet and materials on record, prima facie, a cognizable case was made out, therefore, cognizance of the offences u/s 279/337 IPC were taken and accused was summoned to face trial. 3. Upon appearance of the accused before the Court, he was supplied with copies of charge-sheet and other documents sought to be relied upon by the prosecution and compliance of section 207 Cr.P.C. was made. 4. On 22.11.2022, charge for offences u/s 279/337 IPC was framed against accused. Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial Digitally signed by ANKIT ANKIT GARG GARG Date: 2025.10.25 17:20:38 +0530 and thereafter, the case was listed for PE. PROSECUTION EVIDENCE 5. In the year 2019, I was undergoing treatment from Medanta Hospital, Gurugram as I was being treated for gastromodility. On 07.12.2019, I was returning back to my home from Medanta Hospital in our private car make Grand 1-10 bearing registration no. DL-10CL-7826 at around 11:00 PM. My father was driving the car and I was sitting next to him on the front seat. On our way to home, when we reached subway near domestic Airport, I felt vomiting sensation because of which my father stopped the car on the road side. Thereafter, I had barely opened the car door, one car hit our car from behind. Due to the impact of the collission, I banged against the dashboard of my car. The offending car registration no. is HR-74A4354. I suffered pain ANKIT GARG which was continuiously increasing and my father took me to nearby Manipal Hospital who referred me to Medanta hospital. The driver of the offending vehicle was driving rash and negligently as the impact of the collision was very high which suggests the high speed of the offending vehicle. The collission occurred within one minute since my father parked the car on road side. The offending car was Swift Dezire. I can identify the car if shown to me. texts.arguments: 9. On behalf of the accused, it is argued that the prosecution has failed to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt. The defence submits that the prosecution witnesses have given inconsistent and unreliable versions of the incident. It is contended that the injured witness, PW-1 Adarsh Rathor, admitted during cross-examination that he could not recall whether the parking lights were on, that there was no separate parking area at the spot, and that his father had stopped the car on the main road itself. He further stated that his father did not open his door, that he was himself unbuckling his seatbelt when the accident occurred, and that he did not accompany Digitally signed by ANKIT ANKIT GARG GARG Date: 2025.10.25 17:21:43 +0530 the police to the spot. These admissions, according to the defence, demonstrate that the complainant had parked the car on the main carriageway, without proper caution or visible indicators, thus creating an obstruction that led to the accident. 10. The defence further argues that the complainant, PW-2 Prahlad Singh Rathor, contradicted his own earlier statement by claiming that he had given an indicator and switched on the parking lights, but no such mention is made in his written complaint. He admitted that he gave the complaint after reaching the hospital and that the police did not visit the accident site in his presence. The defence also points out that both PW-1 and PW-2 admitted that the injured was not admitted to the hospital on the night of the accident, which raises doubt about the seriousness and immediacy of the alleged injuries. There is no independent or public witness despite the location being a busy road near the State vs Juned Ahmed on 25 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58676806/ 7 Domestic Airport underpass, and there is no CCTV footage of the incident. 11. It is further submitted that the entire investigation is mechanical and one-sided. The IO PW-3 ASI Jitender Malik admitted that he found no eyewitness at the spot, and that the accused was produced later by the vehicle owner, not apprehended from the scene. No speed estimation, skid marks, or site measurements were taken to prove rashness. The mechanical inspection of the vehicles shows no defect but also no evidence of over-speeding. The defence thus contends that the collision occurred due to the complainant's negligent parking on the road, not due to rash driving by the accused. The accused has consistently maintained his innocence in his Section Digitally signed by ANKIT ANKIT GARG GARG Date: 2025.10.25 17:21:50 +0530 313 statement, stating he was not rash or negligent, and the defence prays for acquittal. 12. On the other hand, the prosecution argues that the evidence on record clearly establishes that on 07.12.2019 at around 11:20 PM, near the underpass in front of Domestic Airport, the accused Juned Ahmed, while driving a Swift Dzire bearing registration no. HR-74A-4354, hit the stationary car of the complainant, causing injuries to Adarsh Rathor. It is submitted that both PW-1 Adarsh Rathor and PW-2 Prahlad Singh Rathor have consistently identified the accused's vehicle and have stated that the impact of collision was severe, showing that the accused was driving at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner. The prosecution points out that both witnesses correctly identified the photographs of the offending car and their own car. PW-2 also correctly identified the accused in court. 13. It is further argued that the site plan and the mechanical inspection report corroborate that the accident occurred when the complainant had parked his vehicle on the extreme left side of a six- lane road, with sufficient space available for the accused to pass safely. Despite this, the accused failed to control his vehicle and collided from behind, indicating rashness. The investigating officer PW-3 ASI Jitender Malik deposed that the accused was served notice under Section 133 MV Act and that the vehicle owner confirmed the accused was driving at the relevant time. The accused also appeared at the police station along with the vehicle and admitted the accident. The medical evidence confirms that PW-1 suffered injuries consistent with blunt-force trauma in a vehicular collision. Digitally signed by ANKIT ANKIT GARG GARG Date: 2025.10.25 17:21:57 +0530 14. The prosecution submits that the defence plea that the complainant's car was improperly parked is baseless, since PW-2 testified that he had switched on the parking lights and stopped the car due to a medical emergency of his son. Even if the car was temporarily stopped, the accused's duty of State vs Juned Ahmed on 25 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58676806/ 8 care under Section 279 IPC required him to keep a safe distance and maintain control. The prosecution argues that the chain of evidence, from the identification of the vehicle and accused, corroboration by seizure memos, medical records, and photographs, forms a complete and consistent narrative, proving the offence beyond reasonable doubt. The State therefore prays that the accused be convicted for offences under Sections 279 and 337 IPC. 15. Section 279 of IPC states that "Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both." To prove an offence under this section, it is necessary that prosecution shall prove that the vehicle of the accused was being driven in a rash and negligent manner. Digitally signed by ANKIT ANKIT GARG GARG Date: 2025.10.25 17:22:03 +0530 16. 20. Section 337 of IPC states that "Whoever causes hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to five hundredrupees, or with both". The accused also cannot be held liable under this section as rashness and negligence of his act has not been proved by the prosecution. Digitally signed by ANKIT ANKIT GARG GARG Date: 2025.10.25 17:22:16 +0530 21.
